source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check the healthy LED
2. Make any error log and check the Healthy LED
3. Clear the error log and check the Healthy LED

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
(Depends on project design)
1. Power-on and Healthy (Green): The system is powered on and healthy.
2. System fault (Amber): System failures, encompassing scenarios such as fan failures, device overheating, and PSU failures.
The Healthy LED changes to green or off once all critical
failures have been successfully rectified.
3. Off (None): None

deepseek_columns.ai_commands:
-- Healthy LED: trigger/clear an injectable error via OOB IPMI and read SEL; the Healthy LED color (green=healthy/amber=fault) must be seen by a person.
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel elist 2>&1 | tail -20
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the SEL tail + BMC health status so the user correlates amber/green Healthy LED; LED color is operator-visual.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: only reads SEL/health; LED color is human visual - agent must not fabricate it.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly separates physical LED observation from SEL collection, but says to trigger/clear an unspecified injectable error while its only literal command reads SEL. It does not prove a causal active health fault, safe recovery or LED priority and exposes a password with `-P`.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires a Project LED matrix, selected safe fault, expected BMC health/SEL transition, protected access, operator observation and recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 814/2291 retains PARTIAL and generic error injection while focusing on OOB routing; it does not resolve whether `error log` means a stored record or an active fault that drives the health aggregator.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-979 draft was inspected only as history. This review independently rejects its MANUAL ONLY classification because the case is hybrid, and explicitly separates preserving/clearing records from repairing the causal fault.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves the fault-transition function rather than reducing the test to read-only SEL; ED-36 treats Project fault/LED values as execution-readiness inputs; ED-38 keeps physical observation, hazardous stimulus and DUT verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Verify the Project-defined physical Healthy LED across three causal system-health states: healthy baseline, an active critical system fault that should drive amber, and a rectified fault that should return the indicator to the approved green or off state. Correlate the optical state with the BMC health model and preserved event evidence.
original_method: Observe the physical indicator at baseline, introduce a Project-approved error/fault condition, then clear or repair it and observe recovery. Because the source says both `error log` and `critical failures rectified`, Review guidance must distinguish a stored log entry from the active condition: deleting a record alone is not evidence that the fault or LED should clear.
manual_activity: A qualified operator confirms the target LED, directly records its color, supervises or performs any physical fault action, verifies the fault is genuinely repaired and checks final hardware state. Automation may apply only an explicitly approved reversible injector and collect BMC health, SEL and domain telemetry.
required_inputs: Project Healthy LED mapping for powered healthy, active critical fault, rectified fault and powered-off states, including multiple-fault priority, debounce/latency and green-versus-off recovery rule

One specifically selected active critical fault class and target, such as an approved redundant fan or PSU transition or safe vendor injection, with explanation of why it drives the platform health aggregator
Exact assert and deassert/repair operations, expected health property and event identity, dwell/timeout, aborts, root-cause recovery and whether SEL cleanup is permitted only after export
Chassis/LED and BMC identity, firmware/SDR versions, independent thermal/power/device monitoring, protected BMC access, operator and synchronized optical/electronic evidence
safety_requirements: Do not interpret `make any error log` as permission to inject an arbitrary SEL record, run `logger`, or create a cosmetic message; the stimulus must be a supported causal health condition.
Do not impair a fan, PSU, thermal or device domain until its redundancy/capacity margin, safe stimulus, dwell, independent monitoring, hard abort and immediate repair are approved.
Export and preserve the baseline SEL and health state. Do not clear historical evidence merely to create a baseline or to make the LED return to green/off.
Treat root-cause rectification and log retention/cleanup as separate operations. Require health deassertion and physical recovery before expecting the LED to recover.
The operator must identify and observe the physical Healthy LED; BMC health or SEL alone cannot prove color, lamp/driver function or front-panel behavior.
Abort on wrong target, unexpected additional fault, thermal/power excursion, host error/shutdown, BMC loss, missing expected event or persistent amber/off after repair. Do not retry automatically.

After repair, verify the selected component/domain, BMC aggregate health, physical LED, host health and retained evidence all recover; perform any approved log clear only after evidence export and never use it to conceal a persistent fault.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate the LED/priority matrix, causal fault-to-health mapping, stimulus, repair, aborts and evidence plan without changing DUT state.

After approval, collect protected read-only baseline/fault/recovery BMC aggregate health, full relevant SEL records and selected-domain telemetry; if the injector itself is approved for automation, execute only that exact bounded operation under operator supervision.
Correlate engineer-supplied physical LED evidence with the actual fault assert, health-state change, root-cause repair and deassert; report log cleanup separately.
Do not invent or physically create a fault, clear evidence, expose credentials, certify LED color, retry, extrapolate one fault to all listed fault classes or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the LED state/priority matrix and one representative fault whose active state is known to drive the health aggregator.
Approve/supervise the stimulus and root-cause repair, identify and observe the physical LED, and own any physical or service-impacting action.
Confirm complete recovery and decide the per-phase and overall DUT verdict; separately authorize any post-evidence log cleanup.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sel elist` is read-only supporting evidence; it neither creates the unspecified fault nor proves aggregate health or LED color, and `tail -20` may omit the causal record. Credential-bearing `-P` form is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, use protected read-only BMC aggregate-health and full filtered SEL/event retrieval plus fault-domain telemetry around the engineer-approved causal stimulus and repair. Do not recommend arbitrary event injection or evidence deletion.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Healthy, error/fault and cleared/recovered phases, Project-dependent green/amber/off Criteria, no Script and 10/5-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Document the healthy baseline; assert one bounded supported critical fault; prove BMC aggregate health and physical LED enter the expected fault state; repair the actual cause; prove deassertion and LED recovery; preserve evidence before any separately approved cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact chassis front-panel health aggregator, LED priority logic and selected fault domain.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/PCA, BMC, BIOS, CPLD/front-panel controller, SDR and selected component firmware/FRU.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project Healthy LED/health-priority specification, selected fault handling and SEL/event definition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns ambiguous log creation/deletion into a causal fault-assert/root-cause-repair sequence while retaining the original wording as source evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only SEL review provides no fault-transition or optical coverage; one selected fault validates only that mapped class/priority, not every fan, thermal, PSU or device failure.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: LED priority/timing, one causal fault, expected health/event, stimulus, repair and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A badly selected fault can reduce cooling or power redundancy; a synthetic event may bypass the real health aggregation path.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select one representative supported fault and define green or off after repair, but must record untested fault classes and cannot claim that arbitrary log insertion/deletion is equivalent to a real critical-fault lifecycle.
expected_evidence: Approved Project LED state/priority/timing matrix, selected causal fault mapping and chassis/BMC/LED/firmware identity
Healthy baseline physical LED media plus BMC aggregate health, relevant full SEL and selected-domain telemetry
Approved stimulus/action timestamp, actual fault assertion and component/domain evidence, amber LED media, matching BMC health and causal SEL/event
Root-cause repair timestamp and component recovery, event/health deassertion, green-or-off LED recovery within tolerance and host stability
Pre-clear exported evidence, any separately authorized log-cleanup record, unexpected-event review, single-fault coverage limits and engineer-owned verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source uses imprecise `error log` wording while Criteria describe active critical failures and rectification. The coherent LED-health lifecycle is identifiable, and an approved Project mapping can distinguish event retention from root-cause repair without AI overwriting source; execution remains unready until that mapping exists.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target, phases and acceptance dimensions are identifiable. The selected causal fault, LED priority and safe repair are Project readiness inputs, so the review can complete without a permanent block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains operator visual evidence and read-only SEL support but supplies the missing causal fault/repair contract and rejects the unsafe credential/truncated-log form.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and sharpens the distinction between event deletion and actual failure rectification, plus single-fault coverage limits.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic injectable-error handling with an auditable assert-health-LED-repair-deassert sequence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects its manual-only classification because approved fault injection and electronic evidence are a meaningful automatable portion, while retaining its warning against arbitrary faults and log clearing.

review_improvement: Prevents a false PASS in which an operator deletes an event record and observes stale or coincidental LED behavior without repairing the underlying fault, and prevents a synthetic SEL entry from being mistaken for coverage of the real health aggregator.
independent_technical_reasoning: This test is about the causal chain from real platform health through aggregation to a physical indication. The optical endpoint requires an operator, but the selected fault lifecycle and electronic correlation can be automated after a package and approval, making it hybrid rather than manual-only. Missing Project values affect execution readiness, not the intelligibility of the review.
